title: Half-Wave Plate
short_intro: A half-wave plate is an optical device made of a birefringent crystal that introduces a phase difference of pi radians (or a path difference of lambda/2) between the ordinary and extraordinary rays. It is used to rotate the plane of polarization of linearly polarized light.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Definition of crystal birefringence, ordinary and extraordinary refractive indices, optical axis orientation, and qualitative understanding of polarization state conversion.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Quantitative derivation of thickness for a half-wave plate, quantitative analysis of rotation of the plane of polarization for incident linearly polarized light, and applications involving elliptical and circular polarizations.

prerequisites: Nature of unpolarized and polarized light
Double refraction in uniaxial crystals (Calcite and Quartz)
Huygens' explanation of ordinary and extraordinary wave fronts

concept_notes.heading: Principle of Birefringence and Wave Plates
bullets: Uniaxial crystals like calcite and quartz possess two refractive indices: n<sub>o</sub> for the ordinary ray and n<sub>e</sub> for the extraordinary ray.

When a light wave enters the crystal parallel to its surface while the optical axis is cut parallel to the faces, it splits into two mutually perpendicular plane-polarized components traveling at different speeds.
A wave plate is cut with its optical axis parallel to the refracting faces so that the O-ray and E-ray travel in the same direction but with different phase velocities.

concept_notes.heading: Action of a Half-Wave Plate (HWP)
bullets: A half-wave plate introduces a phase difference of &pi; (180&deg;) or a path difference of &lambda;/2 between the O-ray and E-ray.
For a negative crystal (like calcite where n<sub>e</sub> < n<sub>o</sub>), the extraordinary ray travels faster than the ordinary ray.
For a positive crystal (like quartz where n<sub>e</sub> > n<sub>o</sub>), the ordinary ray travels faster than the extraordinary ray.

concept_notes.heading: Effect on Polarized Light
bullets: When linearly polarized light is incident on a half-wave plate such that its electric vector makes an angle &theta; with the optical axis, the emergent light remains linearly polarized.
The plane of vibration of the emergent linearly polarized light is rotated by an angle 2&theta; with respect to the incident plane of vibration, in the same direction if &theta; < 90&deg;.
If circularly polarized light is incident on a half-wave plate, the emergent light is also circularly polarized but with the opposite handedness.

concept_notes.heading: Material Requirements and Thickness
bullets: The thickness of a half-wave plate is precisely calibrated to satisfy the phase retardation condition for a specific wavelength &lambda;.
Because thickness depends on wavelength (&lambda;), a half-wave plate designed for sodium light (589 nm) will not act as an exact half-wave plate for other spectral regions.
Quartz is commonly used for constructing wave plates due to its mechanical durability and optical clarity.

derivations.title: Derivation of Thickness of a Half-Wave Plate
derivations.conditions: Normal incidence, light of wavelength lambda, uniaxial crystal with ordinary and extraordinary refractive indices n_o and n_e.
steps: Let the thickness of the crystal plate be t.
The time taken by the ordinary ray to cross the thickness t is t_o = t / v_o = n_o t / c, and by the extraordinary ray is t_e = n_e t / c.
The optical path difference between the two rays is given by Delta = |n_o - n_e| t.
For a half-wave plate, the path difference must equal lambda / 2, or the phase difference must equal pi.
Equating path difference: |n_o - n_e| t = lambda / 2.
Solving for thickness t gives t = lambda / (2 |n_o - n_e|).

derivations.title: Derivation of Rotation of Plane of Polarization
derivations.conditions: Linearly polarized incident light making an angle theta with the optical axis of a half-wave plate.
steps: Let the incident electric field vector be E_0, making an angle theta with the optical axis (X-axis).
Resolve the incident vibration into two orthogonal components along the optical axis and perpendicular to it: E_x = E_0 cos(theta) cos(omega t) and E_y = E_0 sin(theta) cos(omega t).

Upon traversing the half-wave plate, a phase change of pi is introduced between the two components. The emergent components become E'_x = E_0 cos(theta) cos(omega t) and E'_y = E_0 sin(theta) cos(omega t + \pi) = -E_0 sin(theta) cos(omega t).
Let alpha be the angle that the emergent vibration makes with the optical axis. Then tan(alpha) = E'_y / E'_x = -tan(theta).
This implies alpha = -theta, meaning the plane of vibration is rotated to an angle -theta on the other side of the optical axis.
The total angle between the incident vibration direction and the emergent vibration direction is theta - (-theta) = 2theta.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the thickness of a half-wave plate for light of wavelength 589 nm. Given ordinary refractive index n_o = 1.544 and extraordinary refractive index n_e = 1.553 for quartz.
solution_steps: Identify given values: lambda = 589 nm = 5.89 x 10^-7 m, n_o = 1.544, n_e = 1.553.
Write the formula for the thickness of a half-wave plate: t = lambda / (2 |n_o - n_e|).
Substitute the values: t = (5.89 x 10^-7) / (2 x |1.544 - 1.553|).

solved_numericals.question: A beam of linearly polarized light is incident on a half-wave plate. The plane of vibration of the incident light makes an angle of 30 degrees with the optical axis of the plate. Find the angle by which the plane of polarization is rotated.
solution_steps: Identify the angle theta between the incident polarization direction and the optical axis: theta = 30 degrees.
Recall the relation for the rotation of the plane of polarization by a half-wave plate: Rotation angle phi = 2theta.
Substitute the value of theta: phi = 2 x 30 degrees = 60 degrees.

solved_numericals.question: A calcite half-wave plate is designed for a wavelength of 500 nm. If n_o = 1.658 and n_e = 1.486 for calcite, what is the minimum thickness of the plate?
solution_steps: Identify given values: lambda = 500 nm = 5 x 10^-7 m, n_o = 1.658, n_e = 1.486.
Use the half-wave plate thickness formula: t = lambda / (2 |n_o - n_e|).
Substitute into the formula: t = (5 x 10^-7) / (2 x 0.172) = (5 x 10^-7) / 0.344.
Compute t: t = 1.453 x 10^-6 m = 1.45 micrometers.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes normal incidence of light on the parallel-cut crystal plate.
Assumes the refractive indices n_o and n_e remain constant across the entire wavefront aperture.
Limitation: A half-wave plate is strictly monochromatic; it acts as a half-wave plate for only one specific wavelength and fails to do so for a broad spectrum of white light.

common_misconceptions.wrong: A half-wave plate converts unpolarized light into circularly polarized light.
common_misconceptions.correct: A half-wave plate rotates the plane of polarization of linearly polarized light or alters the handedness of circularly polarized light; it cannot polarize unpolarized light.
common_misconceptions.why: Unpolarized light lacks a coherent phase relationship between orthogonal components, which is required for deterministic retardation.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The thickness of a half-wave plate is independent of the wavelength of light used.
common_misconceptions.correct: The thickness is directly proportional to the wavelength lambda.
common_misconceptions.why: From the formula t = lambda / (2 |n_o - n_e|), changing lambda requires a proportional change in thickness t to maintain the pi phase shift.

quick_revision: A half-wave plate introduces a phase difference of pi and a path difference of lambda/2 between O-ray and E-ray.
Half-Wave Plate Condition (Path Difference): \Delta = |n_o - n_e| t = \frac{\lambda}{2}
